cls: Topical skin protectant / mild astringent and sunscreen mineral
pharm: An insoluble inorganic zinc salt used topically as a skin protectant; it forms a physical barrier over the skin that protects against moisture and irritants, has mild astringent and soothing properties, and as a fine particle reflects/scatters ultraviolet radiation, functioning as a broad-spectrum physical sunscreen.
quick: Apply topically to affected/at-risk skin as needed; up to several times daily
Topical use considered safe; negligible absorption
Topical use compatible; clean nipple area before nursing
Skin healing; local irritation or sensitization
summary: Zinc oxide is a topical skin protectant available over the counter, used to prevent and treat diaper rash, protect chafed or irritated skin, soothe minor skin irritations, and act as a barrier against wetness; in sunscreen products it is a broad-spectrum mineral (physical) UV blocker. Applied as creams, ointments, pastes, lotions, or powders (often 10-40%), it forms an occlusive protective film over the skin and has mild astringent and soothing actions. Systemic absorption through intact skin is negligible, so it is well tolerated and considered safe in pregnancy and lactation. It is for external use only; patients should avoid applying it to deep/puncture wounds or serious burns without medical advice and stop use if irritation develops.
indications: Prevention and treatment of diaper rash (diaper dermatitis)
Protection of chafed, irritated, or cracked skin and relief of minor skin irritation
Barrier protection against wetness/moisture-associated skin damage
Broad-spectrum physical (mineral) sunscreen to help prevent sunburn (in sunscreen products)
Adjunct soothing/astringent agent for minor skin conditions and abrasions

dosage.t: With each diaper change / as needed
dosage.n: Change wet/soiled diapers promptly, cleanse and dry the area before applying

dosage.d: Apply a thin layer to the affected area as needed
dosage.t: As needed (up to several times daily)

dosage.t: Reapply at least every 2 hours and after swimming/sweating/towel drying

admin: For external use only; avoid contact with the eyes
Clean and dry the skin before applying a thin, even layer to the affected area
For diaper rash, apply at each diaper change and especially at bedtime when exposure to wetness is prolonged
When used as a sunscreen, apply generously 15 minutes before sun exposure and reapply every 2 hours and after water exposure
Do not apply to deep or puncture wounds, serious burns, or infected skin without medical advice; discontinue if irritation occurs
moa: Zinc oxide is a finely divided insoluble inorganic powder that acts predominantly through physical and surface effects rather than systemic pharmacology. Applied topically, it forms an occlusive, water-repellent layer that protects the skin from moisture, friction, urine, and feces, promoting healing of irritated or macerated skin. It has mild astringent and antiseptic properties that reduce weeping and soothe inflamed skin. In sunscreen applications, the particles physically reflect and scatter ultraviolet A and B radiation across a broad spectrum, providing photoprotection without significant chemical absorption of UV light. Systemic zinc absorption through intact skin is minimal.

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to zinc oxide or other ingredients in the specific product
relative: Application to deep/puncture wounds, serious burns, or signs of skin infection without medical evaluation
monitor: Healing of the treated skin (e.g., diaper rash)
Local irritation, redness, or allergic contact reaction
Signs of secondary skin infection that may need separate treatment

preg: Topical zinc oxide is considered safe in pregnancy because systemic absorption through intact skin is negligible. It is widely used during pregnancy for diaper-area and skin protection.
lact: Topical zinc oxide is compatible with breastfeeding given negligible systemic absorption. If applied to the nipple/areola, wash the area before nursing so the infant does not ingest the product.
renal: No dosage adjustment is required; systemic absorption from topical use is negligible and renal handling is not clinically relevant.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is required; systemic absorption from topical use is negligible and hepatic metabolism is not clinically relevant.

minor: No clinically significant systemic drug interactions from topical use; may physically reduce skin contact/absorption of other topical agents applied at the same site and time
interactions.diagnostics: No characteristic laboratory test interference from topical use.

common: Generally well tolerated; occasional mild local irritation or dryness
rare: Hypersensitivity reaction to the product or its other ingredients
emergency: Severe allergic reaction with widespread rash, swelling, or difficulty breathing (rare)

monitoring: Healing of diaper rash or treated skin within a few days
Local skin irritation, redness, or signs of allergy
Development of secondary skin infection requiring additional therapy
Adequate overall sun protection when used as a sunscreen
counsel: This is for use on the skin only - keep it away from the eyes and do not swallow it
Clean and dry the skin, then apply a thin layer to the affected area as often as needed
For diaper rash, apply at every diaper change and especially at bedtime, and change wet diapers promptly
If used as a sunscreen, put it on 15 minutes before going out and reapply every 2 hours and after swimming or sweating
Stop using and see a doctor if the rash worsens, lasts more than about a week, or the skin looks infected
Stop if you get redness, itching, or swelling that suggests an allergy to the product
pk: Not applicable - acts locally at the skin surface
Not applicable - negligible systemic absorption through intact skin
Persists until washed or wiped off; reapply as needed
Store at room temperature; keep the container closed and protected from extremes
pearls: Classic, inexpensive, and very safe barrier protectant - first-line for diaper dermatitis and moisture-associated skin damage
As a sunscreen it is a broad-spectrum physical (mineral) UV blocker, useful for sensitive skin and infants over 6 months
Negligible systemic absorption through intact skin - safe in pregnancy and lactation and needs no renal/hepatic adjustment
Often combined with other agents (e.g., as calamine, or in pastes with starch) for added soothing/astringent effect
If diaper rash does not improve within about 7 days or worsens, consider candidal or bacterial infection
For external use only - avoid eyes and do not use on deep wounds or serious burns without advice
missed: There is no fixed dosing schedule - simply apply when needed (for example at each diaper change or when skin is irritated). If a sunscreen application is missed, apply as soon as you are able and reapply regularly during sun exposure.
overdose: Topical overdose is not a clinical concern given negligible absorption; excess can be wiped off. Accidental ingestion of small amounts may cause mild gastrointestinal upset (nausea, vomiting); large ingestions of zinc-containing products can cause GI irritation - manage supportively and seek poison-control advice if a large amount is swallowed.
